articles.title: Rs 2,000 crore loss: Delhi traders say protests have hit festive season business - Moneycontrol.com
articles.full_text:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday sought the Centre’s stand on petitions by traders, vendors and lawyers seeking regulation of protests in the capital under the governing standard operating procedures (SOP), TOI reported. The traders have claimed that barricading and demonstrations have already cost them business worth Rs 2,000 crore.
A bench of acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma directed the counsel for the Centre and police to seek instructions before the matter is heard on Friday, the report said. Earlier in the day, the court had allowed urgent listing of pleas by lawyers’ and traders’ associations seeking an SOP for designated protest sites.
The bench also asked the petitioners to place on record copies of the protest-related petitions pending in the Supreme Court. It stressed that it would not “want to cover an area already sub judice in Supreme Court”, the report added. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the government, submitted that the petitions in the top court have been adjourned to October 15.
Senior lawyers for the petitioners argued that the Supreme Court has issued several directions on regulating protests, which also need to be complied with, the report said. Counsel for the traders contended that October to February, being the festive season, is the “best time for business”, and that this period has been badly hit.
The protests at Jantar Mantar kept shoppers away and reportedly prompted traders to seek a shift of the protest site, the report noted. Average footfall at Khan Market in central Delhi and Sadar Bazar in north Delhi was affected, as customers from the National Capital Region largely stayed away. Protest sites have now been designated at Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground.
The New Delhi Traders’ Association in Connaught Place has advised shopkeepers to remain vigilant while deciding whether to open their establishments during the protests. Association president Atul Bhargava was quoted by News18 as saying that traders near the Janpath entry point and Regal crossing chose to keep their shops shut because of frequent unrest in the area. He said this was the only way to avoid damage to shops during altercations between protesters and police, and cited traffic restrictions in the capital.

articles.title: Jantar Mantar row: SFI, DYFI march to reclaim protest site, demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation - Moneycontrol.com
articles.full_text:
The Students' Federation of India (SFI) and the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) held a joint protest march from Firoz Shah Road to Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and seeking to reclaim Jantar Mantar as a protest site.
The protest comes after Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a designated venue for organising protests and demonstrations in Delhi. The Delhi Police has designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as the three new protest venues, according to an official notice.
The announcement of denotification came on October 12, the same day CJP representatives approached Parliament Street Police Station to submit a letter seeking a date and time for their proposed peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations. Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a protest venue.
Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar said a detailed and revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for organising protests and demonstrations at the three designated venues would be issued separately.
The development comes as leaders and parliamentarians of the opposition INDIA bloc launched a massive protest march from Connaught Place in central Delhi, intensifying their agitation against the Election Commission over alleged electoral manipulation and subversion of democratic institutions.
Earlier in the day, Delhi Police said it arrested three Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists, citing alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace, violate the law and instigate others through social media to engage in similar unlawful activities.
Two of them, Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were remanded to five days of judicial custody, while Ajinkya Shinde was bound down for six months to maintain peace and good behaviour.
According to a Delhi Police statement, the action followed an incident on the morning of October 13, when the three activists and 11 other CJP members allegedly entered the denotified Jantar Mantar protest site through private premises.
Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened and attempted to stop them. However, the protesters allegedly obstructed police personnel in the discharge of their official duties, the police statement claimed.
CJP reiterated that its demand for Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation remains unchanged and that it will continue to challenge the denotification of Jantar Mantar. CJP said it would not abandon its demand for electoral accountability or accept the removal of a historic protest venue as a reason to retreat from peaceful democratic action.
